newsitem.title: NORWAY: Aker Maritime designs new oil platform.
newsitem.headline: Aker Maritime designs new oil platform.

text.p: Norwegian offshore services company Aker Maritime ASA said on Wednesday it had developed a new type of floating platform especially suited to smaller fields which previously would have been considered uneconomic.
Aker said preliminary estimates showed that the platform, Buoyform, could be built in 23 months and at around 500 million crowns less than comparable solutions.

Buoyform comprises a conical storage tank beneath sea level and a deck with living quarters and processing equipment above it. It can be moved relatively easily between several smaller fields as each is depleted.

Aker Maritime said that with an 83 metre diameter and a 400 metre draught, the platform's structure has smaller and calmer motions in the sea than either a production ship or a semi-submersible platform.

Unlike a production vessel, Buoyform does not require a turret to accommodate the mooring lines and risers -- tubes bringing produced oil to the surface from the well -- but is held in position with conventional anchor lines.
The combination of drilling, processing and storage facilities avoids investment in a separate storage system and the cost of hiring a separate drilling rig, the company said.
Buoyform also can be delivered as a dedicated drilling platform.
Aker Maritime said the development solutions evaluated so far have a production capacity of 60,000 barrels per day and a storage capacity of 570,000 barrels.
